summary: The study investigates the surface morphology of AlP grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE). It highlights the challenges in achieving atomic-scale flatness and proposes a model based on methyl adsorbate lifetime to explain surface roughness. The results show that controlling the gas feeding time and temperature can improve surface morphology.
evidence: The ALE experiments were performed in a MOVPE system with a horizontal quartz reactor. The metalorganic gas source for the group-III element was dimethylaluminum hydride (DMAH), and phosphine (PH3) was used as a group-V gas source. The growth temperature was 580–590 °C. The surface morphology was observed using atomic force microscopy (AFM).
